title: Counting Bits
prompt: Given an integer `n`, return an array `ans` of length `n + 1` where `ans[i]` is the number of `1` bits in the binary representation of `i`, for every `i` from `0` to `n`.

examples.explanation: 0 is 0 (0 bits), 1 is 1 (1 bit), 2 is 10 (1 bit).

hints: You could count bits for each number independently in O(log n) each, but can you reuse previous answers?
Every number i relates to a smaller number by removing its lowest set bit, or by right-shifting by one.
Use the relation ans[i] = ans[i >> 1] + (i & 1): shifting right by one drops the last bit, and you add back 1 if that dropped bit was a 1.

solution.approach: Build the answer array bottom-up using the recurrence ans[i] = ans[i >> 1] + (i & 1). Shifting i right by one bit removes its least significant bit, whose bit count we've already computed; adding back (i & 1) accounts for whether that removed bit was itself a 1. This lets each answer be computed in O(1) using previously computed results, giving an overall O(n) solution instead of O(n log n) from counting bits independently for each number.
